questions.q: Do we delete the Firebase document-holding design, or adopt it and take the fiduciary and intermediary duty?

questions.stakes: Adopting puts document content under a ₹250 crore ceiling and makes us an intermediary before the first user.
state: Firestore rules cap bodies at 900,000 chars, make revisions undeletable and allow anonymous reads.
The old PRD says we hold documents; the plan says we hold no bytes.
Nothing writes to Firestore; its rules call themselves a prototype.
tension: Holding bytes makes us an intermediary under IT Act section 2(1)(w), which costs 74 founder-hours.
The claim a rival cannot copy is that documents never reach us.

costs: A pilot with no published policy breaches SPDI Rule 4 today

options.system: Firestore becomes the store of record.

options.system: One rule deleted; the duties remain.

questions.flip: If sharing lands on a hosted viewer, (c) is the honest minimum and ₹250 crore must be budgeted.

Costs nothing extra: the Firebase and byte-path decisions point here
costs: Forecloses the web trial and hosted publishing
Removes the likely trigger, not the duty

questions.q: Do we publish a privacy policy, terms and a named grievance officer before the pilot, and which window?

No officer is named anywhere; `privacy` and `terms` are reserved slugs with no route.
tension: Publishing sets it: closed owes one month, open owes 24 hours and 15 days.
We are bound by any window we publish, and missing our own is worse.

options.label: A written notice by hand to each of the ten, full pages in the build after the pilot
gains: Proportionate to ten known participants, and cheap
costs: Does not satisfy the published-policy duty, and anyone can reach the app

It needs revisiting the day publishing opens
options.system: Three static routes and a monitored address.

options.label: Publish the tightest window from day one: 24-hour ack, 15-day resolution
gains: Simplest to explain, and no revisiting if publishing opens

A missed self-imposed window is worse than a modest one
options.system: A monitored inbox with a same-day rota.
options.money: None in cash; real in attention.

options.label: Counsel drafts them first, then the pilot
gains: A reviewed document, covering CERT-In and terms together
costs: ₹40,000–1,20,000 before evidence anyone wants the product
